title: Ghosts of the Void — Authentic NASA Photographic Asset Registry
description: Historical provenance, NASA catalog identifiers, credits, and verification documentation for extraterrestrial robotic relics.

relics.artifactName: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle Descent Stage
relics.depictedSubject: Lunar Module Eagle descent stage at Tranquility Base on the lunar surface. Astronaut Edwin 'Buzz' Aldrin is visible preparing to deploy the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP) from the descent stage scientific equipment bay.
relics.archivalCenter: NASA Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC)
relics.altText: NASA archival photograph of the Apollo 11 Eagle lunar module descent stage on the Moon.
relics.verificationNotes: Directly photographed on the lunar surface at Tranquility Base (0.67408° N, 23.47297° E) with a 70mm Hasselblad lunar surface camera. Depicts the actual LM-5 descent stage clad in gold Kapton and amber thermal blankets.

relics.photographer: Alan L. Bean (Apollo 12 Lunar Module Pilot)
relics.depictedSubject: Apollo 12 Commander Charles 'Pete' Conrad Jr. examines the television camera and surface sampler boom on the Surveyor 3 robotic spacecraft inside Surveyor Crater, Ocean of Storms. The Apollo 12 Lunar Module Intrepid is visible on the crater rim in the background ~160 meters away.
relics.archivalCenter: NASA Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC)
relics.altText: NASA archival photograph of the Surveyor 3 lunar spacecraft.
relics.verificationNotes: Historically authentic NASA archival photograph capturing the only time in human history that astronauts visited and salvaged components from an uncrewed robotic lander on another world.

relics.photographer: David R. Scott (Apollo 15 Commander) / James B. Irwin
relics.depictedSubject: The Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-001) parked alone on the lunar surface during EVA-3 at the Hadley-Apennine landing site, looking north toward Mount Hadley rising 4,500 meters in the background. Shows four zinc-coated wire-mesh wheels, chassis, seats, high-gain umbrella antenna, and TV camera.
relics.archivalCenter: NASA Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC)
relics.altText: NASA archival photograph of the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle on the lunar surface.
relics.verificationNotes: Authentic 70mm Hasselblad photograph taken during Apollo 15 on the Moon. Specifically shows the first Lunar Roving Vehicle driven by humans on another world, with all four wheels and Mount Hadley clearly in view.
